name_reason: Compliant fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> form (domain=cursor, descriptor=move_left). Accurately reflects the function: it is the left-arrow (scancode 0x4B) battle cursor handler. No Ghidra address residue in the name.
purpose: Left-arrow (scancode 0x4B) battle cursor handler: move the cursor one tile left, scrolling the viewport when at the left edge, then composite a fresh frame.
logic_summary: X-axis mirror of fd2_cursor_move_up. After the __CHK(8) stack-probe: if cursor_world_x != 0 (not at map left edge), branch on viewport position. If cursor_screen_x < 2 AND view_window_origin_x != 0 (near left edge with room to scroll): decrement cursor_world_x and view_window_origin_x (scroll view left, cursor stays at its screen column). Else (inner step): decrement cursor_world_x and cursor_screen_x, and if anim_phase == 0 return early without compositing (the main loop redraws on its next tick). All other paths -- the scroll branch, the inner step with anim_phase != 0, and the left-edge no-op (world_x == 0) -- fall through to fd2_composite_battle_frame(0).

returns.semantics: No return value. Side effects only: mutates battle cursor/viewport globals and (in most paths) composites a fresh battle frame.

comment_original_issue: Source comment block was a bare stub (only name/address/caller count) while all three sibling cursor-move functions in the same file carry full descriptive blocks; the actual behavior (left-edge no-op, scroll-vs-inner-step branch, composite-redraw gating) was undocumented in src.
notes: 3 callers: fd2_game_main_loop (keyboard dispatch), fd2_pan_cursor_to_tile_animated (animated pan stepping left), fd2_wait_for_action_target_input (target-selection input loop). __CHK(8) is the Watcom stack-probe prologue (in_stack_* are not real params; the function is void). Ghidra plate already documents the same body and gating and matches the refined understanding, so plate left unchanged. void => params=[].
